title: Dynamics-structure interchangeability in binary opinion models on multiplex networks
abstract: We examine the interchangeability between two duplex systems with opinion dynamics: one characterized by different dynamics parameters $a_1$ and $a_2$ on each layer and full node overlap, and the second with the same parameter $a_1$ on both layers but only partial node overlap $r$. We introduce a general framework for identifying the critical line between the ordered and disordered phases, thereby translating one system into another. The description is supported by several examples of opinion dynamics models and a rigorous measure of the distance between the stationary solutions of the rate equations in both settings. Our results show that even large values of $r$ are sufficient to obtain very good correspondence between the two settings.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to show that the effects of having different interaction parameters on different layers of a multiplex network can be mathematically mapped onto the effects of partial structural overlap between those layers. By analyzing various opinion models, the authors demonstrate a powerful interchangeability principle connecting dynamical heterogeneity to structural disorder.
main_problem: The paper investigates the interchangeability between two duplex opinion dynamics systems: one with distinct dynamics parameters on each layer and full overlap, and another with identical parameters but only partial node overlap.
main_result: A general framework is established showing that dynamical heterogeneity (different parameters) can be formally mapped onto structural randomization (partial overlap $r$) via a derived functional relationship $a_2(r) = f(g(r))$.
method: The analysis uses rate equations derived from the opinion dynamics on multiplex networks, employing the Landau approach to identify critical lines between ordered and disordered phases.
model_or_system: The system is a binary opinion model on a two-layer full-graph multiplex (duplex) network, analyzed using models like the q-voter, q-Ising, and Sznajd models.
key_observables: Total magnetization ($m$), critical lines separating ordered/disordered phases, and the relative distance $D(r)$ quantifying solution correspondence.
important_parameters: Dynamics parameters ($a_1, a_2$), overlap fraction ($r$), and model-specific parameters like lobby size ($q$) and independence probability ($p$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a mean-field approach, assuming the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic comparisons of the two system types, phase diagrams showing the effect of heterogeneity on transitions, and plots quantifying the relative distance $D(r)$ between solutions from the two settings.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the two system settings, develops the general framework for phase transition analysis using rate equations, derives the key mapping equation, and then applies this framework to several specific, well-known opinion dynamics models to validate the interchangeability.
why_interesting: While focused on social dynamics, the mathematical techniques—analyzing phase transitions, mapping between parameter spaces, and using mean-field rate equations—are highly relevant to understanding phase transitions in complex quantum many-body systems.
